title: Pressurized Conduit Discharge

Hnet.description: Net head (reservoir WSE - centerline of outlet or tailwater, whichever controls)

source: General hydraulics — USBR Design of Small Dams

title: Conduit Energy Equation (Full Flow)
equation: H = h_entrance + h_friction + h_bends + h_gate + h_transition + h_exit
alt_form: H = (Ke + f×L/D + ΣKb + Kg + Kt + 1.0) × V²/(2g)

Kb.description: Bend loss coefficient (0.10–0.50 per bend depending on r/D)

Kg.description: Gate/valve loss coefficient (varies with type and opening)

title: Trashrack Head Loss

Kt.description: Bar shape coefficient (1.79 sharp-edge, 1.67 rectangular, 0.76 circular, 2.42 flat)

V_n.description: Velocity through net area (gross area minus bars)

applicability: Kirschmer (1926) formula. For partially clogged racks, increase hL by factor of 2× or more. Design rack structure for 50% clogging case.

title: Air Demand Behind Gate (Empirical)

β.description: Air demand ratio (air flow / water flow)

Fr_gate.description: Froude number of flow downstream of gate

applicability: Approximate — varies significantly with gate type and geometry. β ranges 0.03–0.25 typically. Air vent sized for maximum air velocity ≤ 45 m/s.

title: Reservoir Drawdown Time
alt_form: Discrete: T ≈ Σ[ΔS_i / Q_avg_i] where ΔS = storage change per increment, Q_avg = average outlet discharge at mean pool level of increment

Q_outlet.description: Outlet discharge (function of head, which decreases as pool drops)

applicability: As pool drops, head decreases and Q decreases — drawdown slows over time. Compute in increments (e.g., 1 m pool elevation steps) using elevation-storage-discharge relationships.

title: Entrance Loss Coefficient
applicability: Ke values: bell-mouth (rounded) = 0.04, slightly rounded = 0.10, square-edge = 0.50, projecting (re-entrant) = 0.78. Bell-mouth entrance strongly recommended for outlet conduits.

title: Gate/Valve Discharge Coefficient (Partially Open)

Cd_gate.description: Gate discharge coefficient (varies with gate type and opening)

applicability: Cd varies: slide gate 0.60–0.75, fixed-wheel 0.70–0.82, hollow-jet valve 0.60–0.85 (function of % open). Partial openings experience high velocities and potential cavitation.

title: Conduit Collapse Pressure (Vacuum)

E.description: Modulus of elasticity of conduit material

applicability: For steel pipe under vacuum loading. Full vacuum = ~101 kPa external pressure. Safety factor ≥ 2.0 against collapse. Alternatively, provide air vent to prevent vacuum formation.

title: Hollow-Jet Valve Discharge
applicability: Fixed-cone (Howell-Bunger) valve produces a hollow cone of spray — excellent energy dissipation in free discharge. Maximum head typically 150–200 m. Sizes up to 3+ m diameter.

title: Bend Loss in Conduit
applicability: Kb depends on bend radius ratio (r/D) and deflection angle: 90° miter = 1.1, 90° r/D=1 = 0.35, 90° r/D=2 = 0.19, 90° r/D=4 = 0.10, 45° r/D=2 = 0.10, compound bends: losses are not simply additive if closely spaced.
